If approved, BridgeBio Pharma’s BBP-418—which, according to one Jefferies analyst, boasts “pretty darn compelling” data—would be the first therapy for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. The FDA has an action date of Nov. 27.
As far as regulatory shots on goal go, BridgeBio Pharma has a fairly clear view to the back of the net for a potential November approval for its limb-girdle muscular dystrophy Type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9) drug candidate. If approved, it would be the first disease-modifying therapy for this rare neuromuscular condition.
With an FDA action date slated for Nov. 27, propelled by priority review and no scheduled advisory committee meeting, BridgeBio leadership and advisors alike are confident that the FDA will give the go-ahead due to compelling evidence and unmet medical need.
“This is a profound opportunity to change the course of disease,” Christine Siu, CEO of BridgeBio’s neuromuscular division, told BioSpace , “since our drug demonstrated meaningful improvements in both the ability to walk faster and breathe better.”
Siu explained that patients with the chronic progressive disease lose function over time, becoming wheelchair bound between their 20s and 40s, depending on the aggressiveness of their disease. The condition also causes cardiac and respiratory disease, which can be fatal, she said.
There are over 30 subtypes of limb girdle muscular dystrophy, according to Siu. LGMD2I/R9 is caused by a mutation in the fukutin-related protein ( FKRP ) gene that results in reduced levels of the encoded protein, impairing a cellular process called glycosylation and ultimately destabilizing and damaging muscles. An oral glycosylation substrate therapy, BBP-418 is designed to increase FKRP, which in turn leads to higher levels of glycosylated alpha-dystroglycan (αDG) , a common biomarker for the disease.
Jefferies analyst Andrew Tsai gave BBP-418 higher than 90% odds of approval by the FDA’s deadline, given results from the Phase 3 FORTIFY study , which enrolled 112 patients 12 to 60 years of age with LGMD2I/R9. FORTIFY met its primary interim analysis endpoint, demonstrating a statistically significant increase in glycosylated αDG in patients treated with the drug compared to “approximately no change” in the placebo group from baseline to three months, according to an October 2025 press release . BBP-418 also met the trial’s secondary endpoints, showing an increase in glycosylated αDG and a reduction in serum CK, a biomarker for muscle damage.
Exploratory data from the 12-month interim analysis last month suggest cardiac benefits as well, with 100% of patients treated with BBP-418 returning to normal range for the blood biomarker HS troponin I, an indicator of heart muscle injury.
Not only is BBP-418 slowing the decline of the disease, “you’re actually getting improvement,” Tsai said. “It feels pretty darn compelling.”
‘A real difference’
Presenting clear evidence of improvement means showing that treated patients deviate significantly from the natural history of the disease, Siu said—adding that BBP-418 has succeeded in this goal. The therapy led to a 31-second difference compared to placebo during a 100-meter time test—designed to measure the functional status of muscles involved in the respiratory system—after 12 months.
“That is a real difference for patients between being able to ambulate independently in the community versus being limited to the house,” Siu said. She told the story of one trial participant who was able to walk during her high school graduation, having previously been confined to a wheelchair. “Our drug can make the difference between walking across the stage and being pushed,” Siu said.
Tsai added that the lack of an advisory committee ahead of the FDA’s target date is probably a good thing.
“It’s likely the FDA doesn’t see something in the dataset to tease out, and that it may be straightforward to the agency because it is pretty convincing,” Tsai said, adding that a potential approval could bring BridgeBio to profitability by the fourth quarter of 2027.
The company is now focused on BBP-418’s launch—which would be its second. BridgeBio’s only commercial asset, the transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) drug Attruby, found widespread success after its 2024 approval, and the company has built a similar market force to do the same for BBP-418 for patients with LGMD2I/R9.

“We’ve built out our commercial infrastructure. We have our sales force. We have our medical science liaisons, our field reimbursement managers, and they’re all trained and in the field already speaking with physicians,” Siu said. “Having identified the initial patients who have a genetically confirmed diagnosis, it’s a concentrated market for us at about 150 Muscular Dystrophy Association centers, and we’ve seen a very positive reaction.”
BridgeBio has identified more than 500 prospective patients in the U.S. while guiding toward potentially thousands more given adequate genetic testing and diagnosis. This could make the market opportunity greater than $1 billion annually at peak sales, Tsai said.
Beyond the beachhead, BridgeBio is looking to the horizon with more than 7,000 patients worldwide, approximately 3,000 of whom are in the U.S., with between 4,000 and 5,000 in Europe, specifically in Scandinavia where the causative FKRP mutation has genetic roots, Siu said. BBP-418 holds orphan drug designation from the European Medicines Agency.
Improving access
Pricing for rare disease drugs can be a sticking point, and Tsai noted BridgeBio’s “pricing power” as the potential owner of the first and only treatment in the space. The analyst modeled about $400,000 as an annual list price, “but people ultimately would not be surprised if it were priced at $1 million plus,” he said.
The company has not yet disclosed pricing, but Siu said she and her team are in active discussions with payers, whom market research has indicated are quite receptive to the functional data BridgeBio has shared, along with the unmet need.
Siu said she believes BBP-418 will be priced in line with or comparable to other rare neuromuscular drugs.
Payers will also likely require genetic testing in order to grant coverage, as BridgeBio did before a patient could be admitted to its Phase 3 trial, and Siu expects that to be included in the label. She does not, however, anticipate that it will be an issue.
“Based on the therapeutic hypothesis and the mechanism of disease, there are already two sponsored genetic tests that are broad neuromuscular panels, accessed for free, that can identify not only LGMD but also subtypes that can shorten the diagnostic journey,” she said.
Longer term, BridgeBio is looking to broaden BBP-418’s eventual label to other subtypes of LGMD, including autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy types 2M and 2U, as well as to pediatric patients under 12 with the 2I/R9 subtype.
Other players are also searching for disease-modifying treatments for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy. Industry pioneer Sarepta Therapeutics, which gained approval for the gene therapy Elevidys in 2023 for Duchenne muscular dystrophy, is developing its only remaining investigational gene therapy, SRP-9003, for LGMD2E/R4. In October 2025, the company reported results from a Phase 3 trial showing that SRP-9003 increased expression of the beta-sarcoglycan protein biomarker—a transmembrane protein involved in the αDG complex—by 23.9% among non-ambulatory patients and by 43.4% in those who were able to walk.
Bayer’s AskBio is another contender in the space, with its gene therapy AB-1003 targeting the same 2I/R9 subtype of LGMD as BridgeBio’s BBP-418. AB-1003 demonstrated an acceptable safety profile in a Phase 1/2 trial last October.
However, Tsai said, with a decision date just weeks away, BridgeBio sits comfortably in pole position.

New Google Maps Navigation Feature Could Bring 360-Degree Landmark Guidance
6 photos
Photo: Google
The immersive navigation update announced by Google for Google Maps users earlier this year - and which has already shipped for some users in the United States - includes landmark-based navigation powered by Gemini. The new AI assistant that replaced Google Assistant on Android and Android Auto can look for nearby landmarks and provide drivers with more detailed navigation instructions when heading towards a configured destination.
This means that instead of a typical “turn left in 500 meters,” Google Maps should be able to offer a more detailed turn indication, similar to “turn left after the gas station.”
Google is now getting ready to push this feature to a completely new level.
A patent called “systems and methods for using visual landmarks in initial navigation” describes how this system can provide guidance not only using the landmarks that you find on your route but also the ones that are located at a much greater distance. As long as they can be used for more straightforward navigation, pretty much any landmark can work.
The secret relies on the 360-degree range that this feature would use.
Photo: Google Instead of just looking ahead on your route, Google Maps would consider any landmarks around you.
Google explains in the patent application that “the landmarks the system selects need not be proximate and can include far-away natural objects such as mountains, as well as artificial structures, such as bridges, towers, tall buildings.”
The reason is that these landmarks can sometimes serve as a very efficient way to figure out what directions you must use to continue a route. Google explains that these landmarks can be used not only to indicate the direction you should follow but also the ones you should drive away from.
“Start driving in the direction away from the mountain toward the gas station,” one of the examples offered by Google reads.
Google explains that such landmark information can be obtained by analyzing sets of photos available online.
Photo: Google The analysis begins with the identification of a set of photographs of a landmark and continues by determining a location from which multiple photos of the landmark were captured. Once the system determines the general direction from the determined location to the landmark, it can calculate the right navigation instructions and provide the driver with guidance to continue the route.
One of the most interesting parts of this patent is the crowdsourced component.
Crowdsourcing has become an essential feature of modern navigation apps, and Waze is the most obvious evidence. Using information provided by users, Waze can understand what happens on the road more efficiently, eventually generating notifications for other drivers.
For example, if someone flags an accident on the road, Waze can use this data to issue a warning that is then forwarded to all drivers whose route includes the flagged location. This way, drivers can anticipate traffic hazards and reduce speed in advance.
Photo: Google In this case, Google says that crowdsourced data can be used to determine landmarks that aren’t necessarily visible. Google’s example includes a concert that users reported to be happening nearby.
“Using crowdsourcing or automated techniques, the system can also identify and reference in initial navigation instructions auditory landmarks, e.g. walk toward the music if an outdoor concert is reported at a nearby location.”
In plain English, if someone added a new event either in Google Maps or on Google directly, the system would be able to determine its location and use it for navigation instructions.
“The navigation landmarks can be permanent or transient,” Google says. “The navigation system can generate various metrics for navigation landmarks, and use the metrics when selecting navigation landmarks for certain location and certain orientation. The metrics can be related to observability, prominence, and uniqueness of navigation landmarks,” it continues.
Photo: Google Eventually, Google says that it can rely on multiple methods to determine these navigation landmarks, especially if they are not permanent. Machine vision and other automated techniques and crowdsourcing are some of these solutions that could help, Google notes.
While patents typically point to new-generation technologies that need years to make their way to production, Google’s solution isn’t necessarily years away from rolling out. Landmark-based navigation is already live in Google Maps courtesy of Gemini, and it’s safe to assume that the search giant would continue to explore options to improve this feature using the methods described in the patent.
Google Maps is also betting bigger on crowdsourcing, especially after the traffic reporting system went live on Android Auto and CarPlay in 2024. The more people contribute data in Google Maps, the more such features make sense, but I still wouldn’t hold my breath for an imminent release. The term “soon” has a completely different meaning in the Google world, especially as far as Google Maps and Android Auto are concerned, so it’ll be interesting to see if the company eventually decides to focus more on this idea.

The Classic Land Rover Defender Still Refuses to Die: Defender Classic V8 Is Available in Australia
16 photos
Photo: Land Rover
The fans of the iconic 1983 through 2016 Land Rover Defender from the Land Down Under have received a gift in November: the Defender Classic V8 is available for commission in Australia . That means only two things: exclusivity and high prices.
Land Rover is doing a lot of things lately: electric versions of both the Range Rover and Range Rover Sport, a first-ever Range Rover GT, plus they signed an agreement with Stellantis to make their products in America, with a potential L663-based Defender pickup truck as the inaugural US-made vehicle. Also, the Defender nameplate might also evolve to include a ‘baby’ version, the rumored all-electric compact Defender.
Anyway, these things aren’t interesting for a portion of the Land Rover fan base – as these enthusiasts only have eyes for the older products. No worries, as Land Rover has the Classic division and things like the older Range Rover models and the defunct Defender are still within reach for customers, if they have enough cash in the bank accounts for commission-based creations, that is.
Now, for the first time, the Defender Classic V8 is available to commission in Australia, “offering clients the opportunity to create a Defender tailored to them.” For a price, of course, as adventurers, enthusiasts, and collectors need to shell out at least £209k, which is about $280k at the current exchange rate, excluding delivery and local taxes!
Anyway, the program at least accommodates all wishes. So, customers can choose from any of the classic body styles: the 90 Station Wagon, Soft Top, and 110 Station Wagon, and more versions are set to follow. Customers will benefit from dedicated support from the specialists at Classic Works in Coventry, UK, and Essen, Germany, and Land Rover has created a distinctive Sunset Gold Soft Top as an immediate model for sale, aiming to illustrate “the breadth of personalization available through Defender Classic.”
Each example will be created using donor vehicles originally produced between 2012 and 2016, “fully remastered from the ground up, re-engineered and upgraded,” and featuring a genuine Land Rover 5.0-liter gasoline V8 engine packing 400 hp. It’s paired with an eight-speed ZF automatic transmission, an in-house suspension setup, and Works Bespoke features like modern LED headlights, the Heritage Lighting Pack or Crystal Lighting Pack, and can even be equipped with features like the Explorer Pack.
The latter adds expedition-focused functionality, including a Ply Guys Camper Conversion, “turning the rear space of the cabin into a bespoke living quarter, while a roof-mounted tent box and ladder are also an option for those seeking off-road adventure.” There are also four-piston Alcon brakes, premium leather inside, a 4.8-inch touchscreen infotainment system with wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and more. Cool or not?

Hybrid Honda Passport Throws More HP in Baja Racing Than Any Other 9.0-Liter V8-Powered Trophy Truck
14 photos
Photo: Honda
Without this being a rule in desert racing, it's not uncommon for the custom, high-performance Trophy Trucks to use massive, 9-liter engines to get them over the many obstacles of such competitions.
On average, these powerplants are capable of developing over 1,000 horsepower, and that makes sense, given their size and fittings. But what if I told you a brand-new Baja truck cranks out much more than that from a 2.4-liter engine and some extras?
The vehicle in question is officially called the Passport Baja Spec Trophy Truck, and it was presented by Japanese carmaker Honda just ahead of this year's SEMA show , which opens its doors this week. For all intents and purposes, this is its newest weapon in the fight to land yet another overall Baja 1000 win.
At the heart of the beast is a hybrid powertrain that blends together the merits of a 2.4-liter twin-turbo V6 engine with those of an 800-volt hybrid system. Combined, these bits of hardware should be more than enough to allow the truck to crank out over 1,300 horsepower.
Photo: Honda The vehicle was put together by Honda with assistance from Mason Motorsports, and the engine is not just any other piece of hardware of this kind. I'm talking about an all-aluminum construction based on the engine deployed on the Acura ARX-06 GTP prototype race car, already trialed and tested in some of the world's most demanding competitions, including the Rolex 24 at Daytona and the 12 Hours of Sebring.
Controlling the massive troop is a Masomatic twin-angled drive five-speed transmission put together by Mason Motorsports. Then, the all-wheel drive system has been designed in such a way that it distributes torque through dual rear driveshafts to angled high pinion spiral bevel gears at each wheel, thus eliminating the conventional ring and pinion gear.
A Mason Motorsports differential completes the powertrain setup, running through portal gear sets mounted at each front hub – this solution was chosen so that ground clearance is maximized (we don't have the numbers on what that means).
The Passport is not your standard commercial vehicle when it comes to the chassis either. For this project, Honda and its partners opted for the Mason Gen 2 all-wheel-drive chassis that has been uniquely designed to fit the hybrid setup. That includes, among other things, a unique rear frame section meant to support the V6 engine and hybrid power unit.
Photo: Honda To maintain mass distribution, the truck's fluid tanks and batteries have been installed toward the rear of the chassis, while the 145-gallon (549 liters) carbon Kevlar safety fuel cell has been fitted at the center of the cab.
The bodywork chosen to cover all the mechanical components is made, how else, in carbon fiber, sculpted in such a way as to meet the carmaker's aerodynamic requirements. There are deep side channels behind the front wheels, the exhaust outlets have been installed high up, and they come with aerodynamic fins meant to direct exhaust flow, and tunneling solutions are included into the cab.
The truck makes the connection to the ground with Toyo tires wrapped around wheels of unspecified dimensions. Behind each of them is a suspension system that includes dual Fox Racing shocks of undisclosed capabilities.
Many of the above components and features have already proven their worth in other competitions, including Formula 1 , IndyCar, and IMSA (like, say, the F-1 trialed and tested battery pouch cells housed within a lightweight carbon-fiber case), so it's understandable why the Japanese carmaker is so hyped about all of this.
Photo: Honda Honda plans to line up the Passport Trophy truck on the starting grid for the 2027 Baja 500 race in June 2027 - it's too late for it to take part in this year's Baja 1000. In doing so, the vehicle will become the first-ever hybrid Trophy Truck to take on a SCORE World Desert Championship race. If all goes according to plan, we should also see it line up for next year's Baja 1000.
On top of that, the vehicle will also become the first to go into the competition with what Honda calls an unprecedented suite of electronics and vehicle-control technologies, including dual-axle brake-by-wire, adaptive traction control, and AI power deployment.
Behind the wheel of the monster for the truck’s first race will be two-time Baja 1000 winner Bryce Menzies, with the vehicle to race in the colors of Menzies Motorsports. The pair has a pretty huge legacy to live up to, as Honda has already scored 22 overall and 17 class victories in the Baja 1000, the most of any manufacturer taking part.
There is another aspect of the race we have to consider, and that's the fact that the 2027 iteration will also mark the race's 60th anniversary. Having a truck of this caliber taking part and potentially winning the 2027 edition adds another layer of importance to the next iteration. Naturally, we'll keep an eye on things and tell you all about it.

Saudi Arabia is building the regulatory framework, partnerships infrastructure and IP landscape needed to support a biotech ecosystem, despite regional political instability. Whether it can produce sustainable biotech companies and a resilient manufacturing base for global production remains an open question, but the future looks bright.
Saudi Arabia is making strides to becoming a major biotech and manufacturing player in the regional and global life sciences landscape, but can it fulfill its hopes?
BioSpace heard experts praise recent regulatory reforms, growing international partnerships and a national focus on technology transfer that has bolstered the trajectory of the Saudi science ecosystem. Even geopolitical issues in the Middle East have not overly negatively affected progress.
The next stage of growth will depend on clinical trial and hospital engagement, intellectual property (IP) generation and training experienced biotech leaders.
“Saudi Arabia has the financial resources to build a pharmaceutical manufacturing industry,” said Ravi Kiron, managing director at Biopharma Strategy Advisors. Its next challenge is demonstrating that it can build an internationally competitive biotechnology innovation ecosystem.
Progressive regulatory revisions
One of the most significant developments over the past year has been the Saudi Food and Drug Authority’s (SFDA’s) effort to connect accelerated regulatory pathways across the entire drug development lifecycle, said George Syrmalis, CEO at Bioscience Equity Partners.
At the Drug Information Association Singapore Annual Meeting in September, SFDA CEO Hisham Aljadhey spoke on the integration of the Breakthrough Medicine Program, the New Accelerator Program for Drugs in Rare Diseases (NADR) and the Research and Investigational Drugs (RAID) pathway. Notably, the SFDA CEO highlighted a 20-working-day process for rare-disease drug classification under NADR.
Syrmalis explained this allows clearer and more responsive processes to help companies plan their development programs.
More recently, on October 7, the SFDA and the Saudi National Institute of Health announced five initiatives to advance clinical trials. These measures address practical issues that determine whether a company can run a development program efficiently, Symralis said, such as contracting, identifying suitable sites, establishing research capabilities and navigating regulatory review.
Additionally, Singapore’s Health Sciences Authority signed an MOU with the SFDA on September 14. It covers regulatory cooperation, information and expertise exchange, and exploration of pathways for conventional and novel products, including biotechnology.
“For companies developing medicines internationally, that cooperation has the potential to make development and registration more efficient,” Syrmalis said.
Combined, these announcements can be seen as evidence of increasing regulatory sophistication, Syrmalis concluded.
Robust partnerships
The transition from ambitious investment announcements to tangible execution, is noteworthy, Kiron said. He highlighted Saudi CDMO Lifera’s MOUs with Pfizer, Sanofi, MSD and others, alongside expanding clinical research activity.
“Saudi Arabia is beginning to demonstrate that its sovereign capital can attract international pharmaceutical expertise and build capabilities, although the ultimate test will be how successfully these partnerships translate into commercially sustainable operations,” he said.
An encouraging sign for the life science ecosystem is having institutions such as the King Abdullah International Medical Research Center (KAIMRC) deepen ties with international groups, especially in infectious disease research, said Stefan Wagener, CEO at Biorisk Management International. The Ministry of Health’s BioLabs accelerator, launched under the Kingdom’s National Biotechnology Strategy in its Vision 2030 initiative, has also helped Saudi founders develop research strategies and commercial plans.
“For me, these are practical examples of investment linked to scientific expertise and entrepreneurship,” Wagener said. What remains to be seen is how planned collaborations become active research programs, training opportunities and possibly centers of excellence, for example, in biorisk management, he added.
Having the Riyadh Global Medical Biotechnology Summit in September, despite the escalated regional tension, brought together many cross-border collaborators, said Abdulrahman Alshaya, KAIMRC’s chairman of collaboration and partnerships. Forty-six agreements were signed.
“That shows the global interest is real,” he said.
Manufacturing capabilities
The role of manufacturing is also important, to give local scientists responsibility for improving the production process and for developing IP, Wagener said. “To me, that is how localization builds lasting innovation capability,” he added.
Manufacturing is an important foundation for the broader innovation ambition, Syrmalis said, with the development of technical skills, quality systems, supply chains and experience in operating within a regulated industry. Biomanufacturing is one of the four pillars in the National Biotechnology Strategy of Vision 2030.
“Manufacturing is an entry point, not the destination,” said Alshaya, noting the Saudi leadership’s focus is on technology transfer. He referenced how South Korea moved from electronics into global biologics through decades of sustained R&D investment; Singapore paired manufacturing with discovery through biomedical sciences research and development hub Biopolis and its Agency for Science, Technology and Research.
Geopolitical turbulence impact
Despite recent geopolitical instability, Alshaya said he continues to see sustained engagement with international partners. “To me, that shows global partners believe the current [geopolitical] circumstances are temporary and that things will return to track, even stronger,” he said.
In addition, he noted that South Korea, Israel and Taiwan built world-leading industries under persistent security pressure.
Saudi Arabia’s ambitions can withstand the turbulence, Symralis said, provided the country continues to execute consistently and companies plan realistically for the operating environment. Still, investment decisions may take longer, visits may be postponed and partnerships may require additional safeguards.
“I remain positive about the opportunity, while recognizing that the pace of progress will depend on both execution and the security environment,’” he said.
Practical continuity and resilience are of ultimate concern in biorisk management, Wagener said. For example, a biotech needs to know whether temperature-sensitive materials can reach its laboratories during transport disruptions. Saudi Arabia’s efforts to reroute trade during recent disruptions offer a concrete example of meaningful resilience, he added. That preparedness should be reflected in research institutions and companies as well.
Success considerations and obstacles
“In five years, I would like to see Saudi-founded biotech companies reaching major M&A or IPO stage, multinational firms running real R&D and tech transfer programs here, regulators and investors moving at the same speed and a trained Saudi biotech workforce leading facilities and research,” Alshaya said.
In that timeframe, Symralis said biotech success would mean companies progressing through meaningful clinical milestones, hospitals participating effectively in international trials and Saudi research producing IP that attracts serious commercial interest.
The biggest challenge is building and sustaining the expertise required, such as having an experienced, local team remain through product development, regulatory review and commercial scale-up, Wagener said.
Building experienced management teams, generating and protecting commercially valuable IP and establishing the entrepreneurial culture needed to convert promising science into successful businesses are further concerns, Kiron noted.
Regardless, all experts expressed optimism for Saudi Arabia’s biotech future.
“My genuine belief is that this sector is growing - slowly but steadily - and will continue to expand even more,” Alshaya said. “My message to partners is to be part of the journey and take it one step at a time.”

CHRISTCHURCH, New Zealand — Australian military officials have been furtive about how they will use Anduril-developed Ghost Shark extra-large autonomous underwater vehicles – or XLAUVs. However, they recently lifted the lid on some payloads the Royal Australian Navy is fielding.
In an official unveiling at Anduril Australia’s manufacturing center in Sydney on Oct. 19, three Ghost Shark payloads were revealed.
One entailed sea mines, another was a swarm of Altius-600 loitering munitions, and the third was logistics supply caches.
In other words: Two of the three payloads comprise kinetic effectors to give the Ghost Shark greater bite.
This means a single XLAUV can clandestinely deploy a dozen sea mines, perhaps in maritime chokepoints during a conflict.
Meanwhile, Anduril’s Altius weapons can perform both surveillance and strike.
Regarding the supply caches, an official said, “Let’s just say, people can use their imagination about the sort of forces that would use these on deployment.”
The Department of Defence said in a press release: “The modular design of these platforms allows them to operate a range of different payloads, customized to the required mission.”
Other payloads are being developed for the Ghost Shark, likely involving lightweight and heavyweight torpedoes, as well as electronic warfare.
Ghost Sharks can deploy from shipping containers, off the stern of relatively small ships or from wharves, Minister for Defence Industry Pat Conroy explained.
“It places question marks in adversaries’ minds,” he said.
With Australia having to wait years for nuclear-powered submarines to arrive, autonomous underwater systems like the Ghost Shark can fill capability gaps as six aging Collins-class diesel-electric submarines continue to plod along.
Anduril Australia opened its factory less than a year ago, and “Ghost Sharks capable of a range of complex missions operating far from our shores are now rolling off the line at an increasing rate into the hands of the Australian navy,” Conroy said.
Canberra is spending A$1.7 billion (US$1.2 billion) on its fleet of Ghost Sharks. This amounts to “dozens and dozens” of XLAUVs, but Australia is not saying how many exactly.
The Royal Australian Navy is also fielding the smaller Speartooth XLAUV from Australian firm C2 Robotics.
Navy Chief Vice Adm. Matt Buckley said: “In terms of our platforms themselves, of course they must continue to evolve, and the evolution of modular payloads that we can fit to uncrewed vessels like the Ghost Shark … creates enormous flexibility for us and allows us to adapt these systems to future missions and future requirements.”
He added: “Our purpose is clear – we need to deliver capability at the speed of relevance, strengthen our ability to conduct undersea warfare and seabed operations, contribute to sea denial and help protect our critical undersea infrastructure.”
The Ghost Shark and its payloads have participated in the past few Maritime Big Play Pacific events, including one in San Diego in October.
The first Ghost Shark was handed over to the Australian Navy for testing and acceptance in early 2026.

AIT Worldwide Logistics announced late Sunday night it has acquired Australian freight forwarder Connor Anderson International, giving the fast-growing Chicago-based freight forwarder a significant foothold in the Oceania market and the ability to capitalize on the boom in data center construction there.
Connor Anderson manages air, ocean and road transportation, customs clearance and project cargo for customers, with a large number of technology clients in Australia and New Zealand. It operates facilities in Sydney and Melbourne.
AIT said high-tech customers asked it to expand its capabilities in Australia and that it also expects to win business from the aerospace and automotive industries there. Connor Anderson has helped AIT Worldwide move freight in and out of the country for 15 years.
The transaction will enable AIT Worldwide to securely deliver cloud computing components and other sophisticated equipment required by artificial intelligence companies.
“This acquisition, and the rapid integration that will follow, demonstrates our strategic response to customers in the region and serves as the foundation for AIT’s long-term expansion to serve Oceania more broadly,” said Ray Fennelly, AIT’s chief development officer, in a new release. “CAI’s addition will help our customers scale faster in Oceania and execute complex projects with confidence.”
Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
Why It Matters: Merger and acquisition activity is heating up in the third-party logistics market and AIT continues to be a serial acquirer. Logistics companies are rushing to meet the supply chain needs of AI hyperscalers that require fast and precise freight transportation services.
Last week, Scan Global Logistics in Denmark agreed to buy Portland, Oregon-based OIA Global.
AIT Worldwide is the 43rd largest logistics provider in the world by gross revenue and number 22 in the United States, according to Armstrong & Associates. The company is projecting about $4.5 billion in gross revenue — which includes money collected for purchased transportation costs — in 2026, up from $3.56 billion last year.
AIT started in 1979 as a domestic freight forwarder with a focus on air freight. It now brokers air, ocean and road shipments, provides customs clearance services and warehousing, and has 158 offices worldwide. In February, Greenbrier Equity Group purchased a majority stake in AIT from The Jordan Company and AIT management, giving it greater resources to pursue expansion in key global markets.
Connor Anderson is the fifteenth acquisition AIT Worldwide has made in the past five years. In 2025, the company bought Miami-based forwarder GSDMIA Inc. and Krupp Trucking, a small St. Louis-based forwarder specializing in the transport of high value goods.

Toyota Brings Fresh Adventure-Ready Concepts at the 2026 SEMA Show Under the Woodland Banner
7 photos
Photo: Toyota Motor Corporation
At the 2026 SEMA Show , the Japanese automaker's Toyota Motor North American division is bringing all sorts of things, including of the Woodland variety, as it turns out.
The TMNA division has been pretty busy as of late, showcasing the latest 2027 model year changes for a raft of popular models like the Camry, Corolla Cross, or the Grand Highlander, which just received its own Woodland Edition. But they’re also keeping an eye on everything else, revealing their Toyota Battery Center of North America in Saline, Michigan, claiming the 2026 NASCAR Cup Series Manufacturer’s Championship for the fourth time in its history, or Mazda Toyota Manufacturing achieving the one-million vehicle milestone.
Well, since it’s early November, they’re also ready to come to Las Vegas, Nevada, for the 2026 SEMA Show and, so far, have revealed ahead of the event’s official dates of November 3-6 a little something for everyone. Although it’s not the skiing season just yet, Toyota has already prepared for it with the Snowhunter family of concepts, imagining a complete track-equipped range consisting of five models: Tundra, Tacoma, 4Runner, Land Cruiser, and Sequoia.
Aside from the body-on-frame trucks and SUVs reimagined for deep-snow travel, there was also the GT-S Performance Concept, a reimagining of the Toyota Crown Signia crossover SUV as a “sleek grand touring machine that blends everyday space and comfort with the attitude and road feel of a true sports car.” But that’s not all, of course.
As such, meet the ‘Woodland Vision,’ a family of Woodland concepts that “reimagine how a variety of electrified and family-focused vehicles can be equipped for life beyond the pavement.” There are new versions of the RAV4, Grand Highlander, Sienna, bZ, and Crown Signia ready for prime time, all ready to abandon the city streets at a moment’s notice for “trailheads and campsites.”
CALTY Design Research was in charge of establishing “a cohesive visual and functional identity for the Woodland concepts,” with common elements like “lift kits, large over-fenders, rugged satin-black wheels, All-Terrain tires, two-tone paint on the roofs and hoods, roof racks, and cross bars.” All of them are also dressed in the same Horizon Blue paint, which is inspired by Toyota’s hues from the 1960s used on the Stout, Crown, and Corona.
Set apart, the RAV4 Woodland Plug-in Hybrid Concept and Sienna Woodland Concept reveal Toyota’s electrified and family-focused vehicles taking on a more “adventurous role” within the household; the Woodland bZ Concept brings the Woodland theme into Toyota’s battery-electric lifestyle, and the Grand Highlander Woodland Concept plus the Crown Signia Woodland Concept aim for both “refinement and versatility.”
“United by a shared design language and a common spirit of exploration, the Woodland concepts imagine a future where more vehicles are ready to leave the pavement behind and make the journey itself part of the story,” explains the company, the motivation behind the new concept series.

The Japanese automaker Honda is revealing new prices, effective November 2, for the CR-V and ZR-V compact crossover SUVs in the United Kingdom, one of their most important markets across the Old Continent.

Now, though, it’s time to focus on SUVs in the United Kingdom , where Honda is introducing a new pricing structure for the compact ZR-V and the slightly larger CR-V crossovers, “further reinforcing Honda's commitment to delivering exceptional value alongside advanced hybrid technology, premium comfort and everyday practicality.”
The new OTR (on-the-road) pricing sees the Honda ZR-V e:HEV start from £35,215 (a little over $47k at the current exchange rate) for the Elegance trim, while the Sport and Advance are £37,455 ($50k) and £39,585 ($53k), respectively. Previously, the three models kicked off at £36,525; £38,765; and £40,895, respectively.

Prior to the new pricing changes, they were £48,075 and £51,520 for the e:HEV, or at least £47,795 for the cheapest e:PHEV.

“Honda is committed to delivering great value alongside the quality, technology and reliability customers expect from the brand. This new pricing structure strengthens the appeal of both the CR-V and ZR-V, making our electrified SUVs an even more compelling choice for customers,” explains Michael Doyle, Head of Automobile at Honda Motor Europe (UK).

Restored 1964 Chevy Corvette Selling at No Reserve, Price Already Going Through the Roof
21 photos
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930
51 bids and a top offer that already surpasses $50,000. This is all you need to know about this 1964 Chevrolet Corvette that’s selling at no reserve on eBay. The auction is now in the final two days, and what we know for sure is that the car will leave for a new garage shortly.
The vehicle has already been restored, and this is probably why so many people are trying to get their hands on it. It doesn’t seem to need anything, as it’s in good shape and doesn’t suffer from any rust problems. Before you head over to the comments section to post the typical fiberglass comment, the no-rust promise concerns the frame specifically, which, according to the seller, is as clean as it can be.
This two-owner Corvette was originally purchased by a gentleman named Tom in Las Vegas, Nevada. Tom kept the car for no more, no less than 45 years, and he always babied this Corvette, parking it in his garage in the state of Nevada. This is good news from a rust perspective, as these cars don’t typically struggle with the invasion of rust.
Another gentleman named Ed Watson bought the car in 2009 and immediately started a complete restoration. He spent over $40K to get the Corvette in the condition you can see today. Since the restoration was finalized, the car was parked in a garage, away from anything that could compromise its shape.
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930 Chevrolet produced 22,229 Corvettes for the 1964 model year, and the coupe accounted for only 8,304 cars. With the split-window design now gone, the coupe is less desirable than its 1963 sibling, though the special thing that sets a 1964 apart from the rest of the crowd is the new hood.
Chevrolet also introduced a new Satin Silver finish, while the engine lineup included not one, not two, but four different configurations.
It all started with the base 327, which produced 250 horsepower. The L75 was the first optional engine, being upgraded to 300 horsepower. The L76 and the L84 were the top choices, but despite sporting the same displacement, they benefitted from a higher compression ratio and mechanical valve lifters.
These updates resulted in a notable power increase to 365 and 375 horsepower, respectively.
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930 The L84 used fuel injection and carried an extra price tag of no more, no less than $538. It was an expensive upgrade that only 6% of Corvette buyers ended up getting, so if you somehow come across a genuine L84-powered specimen, you’d better not miss the opportunity to get it.
Otherwise, this Corvette has a period-correct 327, but it is no longer original. We’re not getting any other specifics, so if you’re interested in buying this car, you’d better do yourself a favor and ask more questions before making an offer.
The new 327 is paired with the original Powerglide transmission “that shifts perfectly,” as the owner explains. The car is already in tip-top shape from a mechanical perspective, so you can fly in and drive home if you don’t want to pay the extra shipping costs.
The paint was refreshed as part of the refresh, and the seller promises that you won’t find any cracks or any other problems in the paint or the fiberglass. The interior is also in good shape, and the driver and the passenger seats are said to be in perfect condition.
Unfortunately, this Corvette has also received an aftermarket upgrade, so it’s now fitted with a vintage AM/FM radio with AUX and rear speakers. You can always undo this change if you’d rather prefer to stick with the original settings - and please, do that because these cars shouldn’t get modern upgrades, considering they’re all about those fantastic classic car times.
Photo: eBay seller mcqueen930 The Corvette is also equipped with power steering and power brakes, as well as with air conditioning. Oddly, air conditioning and power brakes were rare options. Air conditioning carried an extra price tag of no more, no less than $421, so only 8.9% of the Vette buyers agreed to pay that much for a climate-controlled cabin in 1964.
Power brakes were significantly more affordable at $43.05, but only 10.2% of the Corvettes ended up being fitted with this special stopping power.
The battle for this Corvette is impressively fierce, and considering this is a no-reserve auction, meaning that the highest bidder takes it home when it all comes to an end, more bidders could join at the very last minute.
The top offer at the time of press is $50,200, and the Corvette landed on the watchlists of $41 people. The listing will go offline in a little over 2 days, so be prepared for some very intense final minutes of the auction.
The car is parked in Winter Garden, Florida, and it should be able to go anywhere on its wheels.

source_document.body:
Former biologics boss Peter Marks had a vision. With the FDA’s latest draft guidance, it’s coming to fruition. Speaking with BioSpace, current CBER leader Karim Mikhail said the “adapted pathway” is designed to develop personalized gene therapies more quickly.
With new draft guidance for the regulation of gene-edited therapies, the FDA has taken a concrete step toward delivering on its promise to expedite the approval of individualized genetic medicines—a promise that has been a long time coming. In fact, it was a vision described by former biologics boss Peter Marks in 2024.
Speaking at the American Society of Gene & Cell Therapy’s 27th annual conference in May of that year, Marks said that one advantage of CRISPR-based therapies is that companies could make many different products that all target different mutations in the same gene, and the FDA could theoretically come up with regulatory processes to simplify the approvals for such groups of therapies.
“There are a lot of nucleotides that can go wrong in the genome. I don’t think we can have three billion visits to the FDA a year,” he joked. “So we’ll have to figure this out.”

“CRISPR constructs can target the liver for a range of conditions, which would be “99.9% identical,” said Marks, who served as director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research (CBER) until he was ousted from the role less than a year after speaking at the conference. That means, he said, you could create a platform that allows you to manufacture CRISPR-based therapies “in a much more facile way.”
Two and a half years later, the FDA has released draft guidance to do just that—streamline biologics license applications (BLAs) to bring personalized gene therapies to patients faster.
“It offers a path for an adapted pathway for these approvals to happen in a more expeditious way,” current CBER Director Karim Mikhail told BioSpace on Friday. Mikhail officially took the top spot at the FDA’s biologics unit in September after serving in the role in an acting capacity for the previous several months.
H.C. Wainwright described it as the FDA turning its plausible mechanism pathway into a “BLA blueprint.” Specifically, the guidance outlines how one regulatory application could cover gene-editing therapies addressing various disease-causing mutations, with the goal of enabling faster access for patients in need.
“Think of the human genome as a massive instruction manual with three billion letters,” Andrew Byrnes, director of the Division of Gene Therapy 1 at CBER, said during an FDA webinar discussing the new guidance. “A genetic disease can be caused by a single typo in these instructions, and different patients with that disease may have different typos.”
The draft guidance proposes the use of a new concept called the individualized feature space (IFS), which describes the parameters for variations on a product to be lumped together as part of a set of customized products.
“The core premise is to create a faster and more efficient access with a consistent ‘individualized feature space’ (IFS) that serves as an anchor for a single BLA . . . that is present across all variations, where each additional variant would need to produce predictable safety and activity,” BMO Capital Markets analysts said in a note to investors on Thursday.
At least two biotechs already have products in development that could benefit from this regulatory approach: Beam Therapeutics and Prime Medicine.
FDA
New FDA draft guidance doubles down on expediting approvals of personalized gene therapies
The FDA has outlined a process for allowing a single application to cover multiple variants of a gene therapy. At the same time, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services has revealed plans to expand the Cell and Gene Therapy Access Model to increase patient access to these products.
October 28, 2026
·
4 min read
·

Read more
Early beneficiaries of the plug-and-play model
Located in Cambridge, Mass., Beam leverages base editing technology, which allows therapies to change single DNA letters directly without cutting through both strands of the double helix, avoiding potentially harmful mutations and cell stress. Beam is using this approach to develop precision genetic medicines for diseases including alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (AATD), glycogen storage disease Ia and phenylketonuria (PKU).
The new draft guidance “converts the individualized ‘product variant’ concept into an operational licensing framework, with base editing the template modality,” H.C. Wainwright said in a Wednesday note to investors.
For PKU, Beam is developing BEAM-304 , currently in a Phase 1/2 trial and designed to correct mutations in the phenylalanine hydroxylase (PAH) gene that cause the disease. In most Northern European populations, there are four specific mutations that cause PKU.
H.C. Wainwright sees the “potential permutations of BEAM-304’s suite of guide molecules” as fitting within the FDA’s draft guidance. “We view the design of the Phase 1/2 study encompassing multiple PKU-causing mutations as a landmark development for the field and prudent for Beam’s base editing therapeutics development in diseases with multiple disease-causing mutations,” the analysts wrote.
Another potential beneficiary of the FDA’s new framework is Prime Medicine, BMO said on Thursday. The biotech is developing genetic medicines based on prime editing, which, like base editing, avoid double-strand breaks cuts to enable high-precision changes to the DNA.
Prime’s platform-based approach “is poised to benefit,” the analysts continued, particularly in Wilson disease, for which the company is developing PM577a for variants of the disease caused by an H1069Q mutation in the ATP7B gene—the most common causative mutation of the progressive genetic disorder in North America and Europe, according to Prime. The asset, which is intended as a one-time treatment to correct this mutation, is currently in a Phase 1/2 trial .
“PM577a targets H1069Q and follow-on editors could address other ATP7B variants using largely common delivery and editing components,” BMO said. “FDA’s draft guidance could provide an important regulatory tailwind for Prime Medicine by allowing subsequent mutation-specific editors to rely primarily on laboratory evidence once a shared platform and clinically predictive acceptance criteria are established.”
The FDA’s concept could extend much further than Beam and Prime in the future. As Mikhail noted, researchers are uncovering new mutations every day.
“The pace of the innovation in the science is incredible,” Mikhail said. “In gene therapy, you have eight to 10 mutations being discovered a week.”
A unified rare disease journey
Over the last two years, through unprecedented FDA turnover , rare disease has been a primary focus at CBER. Marks had long championed regulatory innovation to support the advancement of gene therapies, overseeing the approvals of Novartis’ spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy Zolgensma, Sarepta’s Duchenne muscular dystrophy gene therapy Elevidys and Vertex and CRISPR Therapeutics’ Casgevy for sickle cell disease.
After Marks resigned in March 2025, Vinay Prasad took the reins in May, and alongside then FDA Commissioner Marty Makary, developed a new regulatory pathway for rare disease drugs, allowing for their conditional approval based on a “scientifically plausible mechanism.” This initiative moved down the field another yard in November last year, when Makary and Prasad further elucidated the pathway in an article in The New England Journal of Medicine .
Makary and Prasad both left the agency in the spring, and a new set of leaders have picked up the torch. Acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas alongside Mikhail and Michael Davis as director of the Center for Drug Evaluation and Research introduced the Rare Disease Framework Initiative , aimed at standardizing the agency’s approach to scientific evidence in this space.
“We’ll be standing up the work streams pretty aggressively on a rapid timeline,” Davis told BioSpace on Friday, adding that time is of the essence. During a public meeting this week to discuss the framework, he added, “you could hear from patients and families that they can’t wait.”

McLaren McL 6GT Makes Global Public Debut in Las Vegas, Brits Announce a McL 820 Supercar for 2027
7 photos
Photo: McLaren Automotive
McLaren has been pretty busy lately, which is spectacular for an exotic supercar company, and we now know more about its future plans, including the long-rumored SUV and a new production supercar called the McLaren McL 820.
The fall season has been pretty fruitful for the exotic British company. For example, the new McLaren W1 was announced for the Forza Horizon 6 video game back in September. Still, more importantly, that same month revealed a new McLaren Automotive investment worth £500 ($670) million from shareholder L’IMAD to create “an integrated UK operation spanning design, engineering, advanced manufacturing and vehicle development, while enabling McLaren Automotive to build engines in-house in the UK for the first time in its history.”
McLaren immediately marked the new business chapter with “the reveal of an evolved identity” featuring a new McLaren wordmark alongside the now classic Speedmark, Papaya, and Speedy Kiwi elements of brand identity. Sadly, October came with bad news at first: the company took the final orders for the McLaren 750S , “bringing the curtain down on a supercar platform that has been one of the most iconic and successful of its generation.” The 750S will bow out of production in 2027, a decade since the 720S predecessor was introduced.
No worries, though, as McLaren has plans to compensate for the loss: following its initial private reveal during the 2026 Monterey Car Week in California, the brand-new McLaren McL 6GT made its global public debut in Las Vegas, Nevada. It wasn’t at the legendary SEMA Show , despite all eyes being on it. Instead, the McLaren McL 6GT was introduced in front of the general audience at the 2026 Concours at Wynn Las Vegas (October 29 through November 2).
Based on “Bruce McLaren’s original, but unfulfilled supercar dream,” the McL 6GT focuses on McLaren's heritage more than anything else with a “lightweight carbon-fiber construction, V8 internal combustion power, and for the first time in a McLaren since the legendary McLaren F1, an authentic manual transmission sending drive to the rear wheels.” The McL 6GT will begin production in 2028 as “a newly positioned and highly exclusive type of McLaren supercar beyond the core supercar line and newly announced SUV.”
More importantly, at the same time McLaren has also announced the McL 820 as the next McLaren series supercar, coming next year, and to commemorate the announcement, McLaren brought a kiwi bird statue to central London, completely wrapped in camouflage but also featuring the new name on it. “First used by Bruce McLaren, the kiwi represents a defining part of McLaren’s heritage,” and the company is now using it while looking toward the future. The new model has the McL prefix, inspired by McLaren's motorsport heritage, and also the classic performance-driven numerical identifier.
That means we already know the exact power of the McL 820, which is 820 ps, or 809 horsepower. “The naming convention marks the next chapter in McLaren's evolution, creating a clearer and more consistent approach that unifies cars across McLaren Automotive and Racing,” says the company. Quite obviously, this also means the new McLaren McL 820 is the direct successor to the 720S and 750S models.
“There is something uniquely special about McLaren. Throughout our history, we've never been content to follow established paths. We've always looked ahead, driven by a restless desire to innovate, create and push beyond expectations,” said David Woodhouse, Chief Creative Officer, McLaren Automotive, when they introduced the new brand identity. Let’s see how that philosophy applies to the new generation of supercars.

At OCP Global Summit 2026 in San Jose, we stopped by the ASRock Rack booth and saw a broad set of NVIDIA systems. That included a full NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 rack. Next to it were HGX Rubin NVL8 servers in both 2U and 5U, two NVIDIA MGX RTX PRO servers, and a dual NVIDIA Vera CPU server. We also spotted the liquid-cooled NVIDIA Spectrum-X SN6600-LD switch and the passively cooled NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPU.
A big theme was liquid cooling. ASRock Rack used direct-to-chip liquid cooling on its rack-scale system and HGX servers, including an 8x RTX PRO 6000 PCIe server.
ASRock Rack XGMRACK-VR/NVL72 NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72
The XGMRACK-VR/NVL72 is ASRock Rack’s version of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72. It is a 48RU NVIDIA MGX rack with a 5000A busbar and a liquid manifold. Inside are 18 Vera Rubin compute trays and nine NVLink 6 switch trays, for a total of 36 NVIDIA Vera CPUs and 72 NVIDIA Rubin GPUs.
ASRock Rack OCP Summit-XGMRACK-VR-NVL72N 5
NVIDIA lists the full rack at 3,600 PFLOPS of NVFP4 inference (sparse) and 2,520 PFLOPS of NVFP4 training (dense). It has 20.7TB of HBM4, and each Rubin GPU gets 288GB. Power comes from four 3RU 19″ power shelves. Each shelf is rated at 110kW and uses six 18.3kW PSUs plus bulk capacitors. ASRock Rack offers in-rack, in-row, RDHx, or liquid-to-air sidecar CDU options.
ASRock Rack OCP Summit-XGMRACK-VR-NVL72N 1
Each compute tray is a 1U NVIDIA MGX design with two Vera Rubin Superchips. Each Superchip connects two Rubin GPUs to one Vera CPU over NVLink-C2C. Networking is eight 800Gbps OSFP ports from NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs, plus two 400Gbps QSFP112 ports from an NVIDIA BlueField-4 DPU. There are even management switches up top for the lower-speed networking.
ASRock Rack OCP Summit-XGMRACK-VR-NVL72N 2
The trays are fully liquid-cooled, which helps lower the total power consumption in the rack, and is something that NVIDIA has been advancing along with its partners for a few generations now.
For those who want a more traditional HGX 8-GPU form factor, there were options for that as well, but with a twist.
ASRock Rack 2U16X-GNR2/DLC RUBIN with NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8
The 2U16X-GNR2/DLC RUBIN was one of the most impressive systems at the booth. It puts an NVIDIA HGX Rubin NVL8 board, with eight Rubin GPUs, into a 2U chassis. It is fully liquid-cooled, covering the E1.S drives, CPUs, and GPUs, with no fans. Networking includes NVIDIA ConnectX-9 SuperNICs and BlueField-4 DPUs. Power comes in over a 54V DC busbar.
ASRock Rack OCP Summit-2U16X-GNR2_DLC RUBIN 2
The host is a dual-socket Intel Xeon 6 platform. It supports the Xeon 6700P, 6500P, and 6700E series in LGA 4710 sockets, with 16+16 DIMM slots at 2DPC. While it supports other series, given the cost of the rest of the system, we would imagine the vast majority of folks buying these will opt for the Xeon 6700P series.
ASRock Rack OCP Summit-2U16X-GNR2_DLC RUBIN 15
There are eight 800Gbps OSFP ports via NVIDIA ConnectX-9, along with 8x hot-swap E1.S NVMe bays. NVIDIA quotes 400 PFLOPS of NVFP4 compute (sparse) for HGX Rubin NVL8.
ASRock Rack OCP Summit-2U16X-GNR2_DLC RUBIN 16
The HGX 8-GPU platform underwent major changes in this generation, including a change in GPU orientation in the tray. This change enables it to work in high-density, liquid-cooled racks.
There was more in the booth, including hybrid-cooled servers, so let us get to those next.

Supreme Lamborghini Gallardo Restomod by Giugiaro Costs a Million Bucks, Donor Car Not Included
28 photos
Photo: GFG Projetti
Did the automotive world genuinely need a restomodded Lamborghini Gallardo in 2026, exactly 28 years after Fabrizio Giugiaro first sketched its razor-sharp wedge silhouette in 1998? Purists might argue that tampering with Sant'Agata Bolognese's ultimate volume-seller is borderline heresy, a cynical exercise in nostalgia aimed at deep-pocketed collectors chasing carbon-fiber vanity.
Yet, when the original architect himself picks up the pencil again, the conversation immediately shifts from sacrilege to redemption.
Unshackled from turn-of-the-millennium corporate bean-counters and industrial manufacturing compromises, Giugiaro decided his mid-engine creation deserved a ferocious upcycle. That explosive ambition materialized at the Concours at Wynn Las Vegas, where Giugiaro's Moncalieri-based GFG Style and CAVËN Atelier unveiled the Hommage 26.
Arriving seven days after the hand-beaten copper Peralta D coupé in Mexico and months after the Bizzarrini 5300 Aperta Lusso, the bright orange Lambo lookalike inaugurates CAVËN Atelier's Designer Series.
The official press release’s deliberate omission of the name of the vehicle that sired this Hommage a clever way to avoid trademark friction. However, the photographs leave zero doubt that the first-generation Lamborghini Gallardo stands at the foundation of this machine. Its cab-forward stance, steeply raked windshield, roofline arc, and compact mid-ship proportions are unmistakable signatures of Giugiaro's 1998 Italdesign proposal.
Photo: GFG Projetti While retaining those foundational bones, GFG Style replaced every single exterior panel with bespoke carbon-fiber bodywork, pulling the surfaces tighter and carving much more aggressive creases. Dressed in blazing orange with a contrasting black greenhouse, the nose preserves the vertical headlamp architecture of the original car. Critics immediately mocked it for the running mascara face, but that’s up to personal taste, so it’s beyond objective argumentation.
Crucially, the Hommage 26 finally realizes Giugiaro's 1998 vision of linking the headlights and gaping lower intakes through a concealed dual-bar horizontal LED lighting system. In profile, the supercar crouches over bespoke 20-inch five-spoke alloy wheels that frame an upgraded braking system, while deeply sculpted rockers feed reprofiled side cooling ducts.
Overhead, the black roof flows continuously into a louvered engine bay cover, culminating in an integrated rear spoiler flanked by two active aerodynamic side flaps. Giugiaro also engineered a new opening rear cabin window specifically to funnel raw exhaust acoustics directly inside the cockpit.
Photo: GFG Projetti The rear view represents the boldest visual departure from the donor supercar. A full-width black mesh fascia houses vertical twin-slat LED taillights paired with horizontal light blades, sitting above a sculpted diffuser and two wide rectangular tailpipes flanking the custom license plate.
Inside the cockpit, the overhaul continues with fresh instrument graphics and completely redesigned seats built to increase both lateral comfort and driving ergonomics.
Beneath the slatted decklid beats the naturally aspirated 5.0-liter V10 engine, thoroughly reworked by the wizards at Italtecnica to scream all the way to an 8,500 rpm redline. Buyers can specify the ten-cylinder powerhouse in a GT configuration producing 540 PS (533 hp) or a flagship Performance specification delivering 560 PS (552 hp). Power hits the tarmac exclusively through a traditional gated manual gearbox. Yes, 6-speed.
Photo: GFG Projetti To harness that high-revving fury, GFG Style equipped the chassis with a new electronically controlled suspension featuring selectable Comfort and Sport damping modes. Production is capped at 25 numbered examples worldwide, and you can’t simply walk into a showroom and place and order for it. you either bring a Gallardo along to be transmuted into a Hommage 26, or you designate CAVËN Atelier to source one.
Sounds easy, right? Well, the upcycling of a 2000s Lamborghini will set you back a cool €900,000. That’s a million bucks (and small change) at the November 1, 2026 exchange rate. That’s a fully loaded Revuelto SV (Super Veloce) with Ad Personam goodies bolted onto it. And it doesn't account for the extra $150K needed for the Gallardo donor car. Talk about restomods throwing the bank account under the bus.
Photo: GFG Projetti Compared to the stock first-generation Gallardo, the Hommage 26 sheds weight via carbon-fiber construction, introduces active rear aerodynamics, sharpens handling, and extracts up to 60 PS (59 hp) more from the 5.0-liter block.
Manufactured in Sant'Agata Bolognese from 2003 to 2013, the Lamborghini Gallardo amassed 14,022 units across a 10-year run, cementing its status as the brand's first production V10 and best-selling supercar of its era. Its expansive lineup included the Coupé, Spyder, SE, Nera, Superleggera, rear-wheel-drive LP 550-2 Valentino Balboni, LP 560-4, LP 570-4 Superleggera, Super Trofeo Stradale, and Squadra Corse. Neat lineage, and a lot of shoes for the Hommage 26 to fill.
Across that decade, Lamborghini deployed two distinct naturally aspirated V10 powerplants. First-generation cars built from 2003 to 2008 carried an even-firing powerhouse rated between 500 PS (493 hp) and 530 PS (523 hp). The 2008 facelift introduced a direct-injected, odd-firing 5.2-liter (5,204 cc) V10 delivering between 550 PS (542 hp) and 570 PS (562 hp). Both generations offered a 6-speed Graziano manual gearbox or a 6-speed e-gear automated sequential transmission.
Photo: GFG Projetti In 2003, the base Gallardo Coupé packed 500 PS (493 hp) and 510 Nm (376 lb-ft), sprinting from 0 to 100 kph (62 mph) in 4.2 seconds toward a 309 kph (192 mph) top speed, all for only $165,900. Conversely, the flagship 2013 LP 570-4 Squadra Corse boasted 570 PS (562 hp) and 540 Nm (398 lb-ft), hitting 100 kph (62 mph) in 3.4 seconds, reaching 325 kph (202 mph), and starting at $259,100.
Notably, the exact even-firing 5.0-liter V10 with 88 mm (3.46 in) cylinder bore spacing utilized in the Hommage 26 remained exclusive to Sant'Agata Bolognese, powering only the 1995 Giugiaro-styled Calà concept and 2003 to 2008 Gallardo models. However, its redesigned 5.2-liter successor powered the Lamborghini Huracán, Audi R8, C6 Audi S6, D3 Audi S8, and Italdesign Zerouno, while inspiring the twin-turbocharged 5.0-liter V10 in the ferocious C6 Audi RS6.
So, its this Hommage 26 a grand finale, a majestic throwback to a masterpiece, or a tentative “teach an old dog new tricks” act? After all, a million bucks for a V10 from 25 years ago with new makeup isn’t likely to become the holy grail Lamborghini Gallardo “What If” fans would throw money at. With companies including AstraZeneca, Pfizer and Revolution Medicines clamoring to get in on Summit Therapeutics’ Akeso-partnered PD-1xVEGF antibody, one analyst calls the asset “the next major backbone” of cancer treatment.
Summit Therapeutics’ Akeso-partnered PD-1xVEGF bispecific antibody ivonescimab finds itself at the center of a cancer collaboration craze, with some of biopharma’s biggest names lining up for a chance to hook their respective assets onto what could possibly be oncology’s next big thing.
After besting Merck’s mega-blockbuster Keytruda in a China-based head-to-head Phase 3 study in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) in September 2024, “ivonescimab pretty much set the world on fire,” Graig Suvannavejh, managing director and senior biotech and biopharma analyst at Mizuho Securities, told BioSpace in an email interview.
Keytruda inhibits the PD-1 pathway, which prevents cancer cells from evading and weakening the immune system’s anticancer response. Adding a VEGF mechanism on top of this additionally stops the formation of new blood vessels, starving the tumor. The PD-1xVEGF market could exceed $30 billion by 2032, according to Vision Lifesciences.
A telling readout from a global Phase 3 trial testing ivonescimab versus Keytruda as a frontline treatment option for NSCLC is set to drop “any day now,” Suvannavejh noted.
“If ivonescimab ultimately lives up to its billing of being better than Keytruda,” he said, the asset “theoretically could stand to become the next major backbone of treatment in cancer in the future.”
This notion is not lost on other drugmakers. Many leading biopharma companies have entered into clinical trial collaborations with Summit, hoping to package their products into combo regimens with ivonescimab.
“Organizations have increasingly approached us about partnering on clinical studies evaluating ivonescimab in combination regimens,” Dave Gancarz, chief business and strategy officer at Summit, told BioSpace in an email. Other companies with active clinical trial collaborations to pair their drugs with ivonescimab include AstraZeneca and Revolution Medicines. Gancarz said that this activity reflects broad scientific interest in the drug’s potential as an immunotherapy backbone across multiple tumor types and treatment settings.
Lung cancer
Summit Declares NSCLC Victory Over Keytruda, Analysts Advise Caution With China-Only Data
In advanced non-small cell lung cancer, Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab appears to be 49% more effective at reducing the risk of disease progression or death versus Merck’s Keytruda in a late-stage study. However, analysts contend the caveat is that the trial was conducted in an entirely Chinese patient population.

AstraZeneca in particular has bought into Summit and ivonescimab. Not only has the British-Swedish heavyweight struck two separate clinical trial collaborations with the biotech, it recently gave Summit a $2 billion equity investment .
“The completed equity investment gives AstraZeneca direct economic participation in Summit’s future value creation across the broader ivonescimab opportunity, not only potential combinations with AstraZeneca medicines,” a company spokesperson told BioSpace in an email.

Summit snags $2B investment from AstraZeneca, clearing financial overhang
The all-stock deal gives Summit Therapeutics enough money to see through Phase 3 trials for the PD-1/VEGF bispecific ivonescimab—but keeps the asset fully in-house without giving up licensing rights.

Pharma powerhouses and rising stars
It’s too early to say how big ivonescimab could become in the cancer space, Dara Azar, associate vice president of Biotech Equity Research at Stifel, told BioSpace in an email interview, “but it looks like AstraZeneca didn’t want to wait.”
Most recently, the pharma and partner Daiichi Sankyo inked a clinical trial collaboration to evaluate their TROP2-targeting antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) Datroway alongside ivonescimab in multiple tumor types. The collaboration will kick off with a late-stage study in first-line triple-negative breast cancer, though the companies haven’t specified a start date.
And just days before the Datroway deal, AstraZeneca announced a separate clinical trial collaboration with Summit that will combine ivonescimab with its anti-CLDN18.2 ADC sonesitatug vedotin (sone-ve). The agreement focuses on gastrointestinal cancers, with studies set to begin “imminently,” the pharma said.
Part of why AstraZeneca has pushed so hard with ivonescimab combo deals, Azar said, could be because many of its peers were already in the PD-1xVEGF race. Merck in November 2024 paid $588 million upfront and put an additional $2.7 billion on the line to exclusively license LaNova Medicines’ PD-1xVEGF bispecific LM-299. Pfizer, meanwhile, has also started building out its PD-1xVEGF pipeline, betting up to $6 billion in May 2025 to advance 3SBio’s SSGJ-707, now named PF-08634404 and in multiple clinical trials across urothelial carcinoma, NSCLC and renal cell carcinoma, among other cancer types.
Already having a PD-1xVEGF doesn’t mean these pharmas aren’t also considering an ivonescimab combo. Three months before inking the 3SBio pact, Pfizer entered into a clinical trial collaboration with Summit to test ivonescimab with “several” of its ADCs for various solid tumor indications. Pfizer is putting forward its vedotin ADCs, most of which it obtained in the $43 billion acquisition of Seagen in 2023. This class includes its FDA-approved Padcev, indicated for urothelial cancer , and sigvotatug vedotin, in Phase 3 development for NSCLC.
Ivonescimab’s appeal also extends beyond Big Pharma. In June 2025, Revolution Medicines—which recently secured FDA approval for its pancreatic cancer drug Rasonque— offered its array of RAS(ON) inhibitors, including Rasonque, as potential combination partners for ivonescimab. This clinical trial tie-up also includes the investigational G12D-selective and G12C-selective inhibitors zoldonrasib and elironrasib, respectively.

But ivonescimab earned its “Keytruda killer” nickname for a reason. While an overall survival miss in a global Phase 3 study in May 2025 dampened sentiment surrounding the bispecific’s competitive value, many still believe that ivonescimab will ultimately be a more effective treatment than Merck’s.
“Investors expect this drug to ultimately be proven as the better checkpoint inhibitor,” Stifel’s Azar told BioSpace .
Ivonescimab is currently under FDA review as a second-line treatment for patients with advanced non-squamous NSCLC, with a decision expected Nov. 14 . Looking at ivonescimab’s body of data so far, Azar doesn’t expect the drug to run into any major regulatory issues.
AstraZeneca is a bit more reserved when it comes to ivonescimab. “It is important to be balanced about the evidence,” the spokesperson said. “Much of the positive data to date comes from China-only trials, and we recognize that single-region data have more limited relevance to populations outside China.”
Indeed, ivonescimab’s current application is backed by the Phase 3 HARMONi trial, which hinted at slight differences in the drug’s efficacy between Asian and Western patients. Summit did not provide statistical analyses for the survival benefit seen in HARMONi, however. The AstraZeneca spokesperson said ivonescimab will need to show that it can significantly improve overall survival in global patient populations to credibly support an approval bid outside of China.
More Western data should be coming soon. Summit is anticipating final progression-free survival (PFS) data from the Phase 3 multiregional HARMONi-3 study testing ivonescimab versus Keytruda as a frontline treatment option for NSCLC before the end of the year.
“All eyes are focused on the announcement of Phase 3 HARMONi-3 study data,” Suvannavejh said.
“If the data do pan out,” he continued, “then simply put, ivonescimab has the potential to replace Keytruda as the next major backbone of treatment in cancer—and in turn, to become the next best-selling oncology drug of all time.”
